mechanism_narrative: The joint recovery of TRANSIT and WORKPLACES toward baseline indicates commuters and office workers are resuming out-of-home routines; this raises weekday retail footfall, so RETAIL_REC will be higher over the next 28 days than over the last 28 days.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC next 28-day mean is not higher than its last 28-day mean despite TRANSIT and WORKPLACES continuing to improve for at least two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A TRANSIT weekly mean crossing above -10 percent indicates that capacity limits and travel advisories have stopped binding; retail and recreation trips then accelerate, producing a higher RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT weekly mean rises above -10 percent change from baseline.
failure_condition: TRANSIT crosses above -10 but RETAIL_REC over the following 14 days does not exceed its level in the preceding 14 days.

mechanism_narrative: When PARKS stays above 60 and RESIDENTIAL drops below 2, residents are moving outdoor leisure back toward normal and spending less time at home; this outdoor orientation spills into retail trips, lifting RETAIL_REC over the next 7 days.
candidate_trigger: PARKS > 60 and RESIDENTIAL < 2 in the same week.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 7 days is lower than its prior 7-day mean in weeks where PARKS > 60 and RESIDENTIAL < 2.

mechanism_narrative: In a partial office-return regime, WORKPLACES between -25 and -15 signals that downtown offices are repopulating without a return to full capacity; nearby retail and recreation venues capture after-work spending, so RETAIL_REC rises over the next 14 days.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES weekly mean remains between -25 and -15 percent.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC falls or stays flat over the next 14 days while WORKPLACES remains between -25 and -15.

mechanism_narrative: The summer-to-autumn transition reduces PARKS mobility from its peak; when PARKS falls below 50, displaced outdoor leisure demand shifts toward indoor retail and food venues, lifting RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days.
candidate_trigger: PARKS weekly mean falls below 50 percent change from baseline.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is not higher than its last 28-day mean after PARKS falls below 50.

mechanism_narrative: A GROCERY_PHARM weekly mean above +10 signals precautionary restocking and health-supply trips; this diverts household spending from discretionary retail, so RETAIL_REC declines over the next 7 days.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM weekly mean exceeds +10 percent change from baseline.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 7 days is higher than its prior 7-day mean when GROCERY_PHARM is above +10.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT remains below -20 while WORKPLACES rises above -20, commuting recovery is narrow and does not restore broad footfall; retail and recreation activity stalls, so RETAIL_REC falls over the next 14 days.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT < -20 and WORKPLACES > -20 in the same week.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 14 days despite TRANSIT < -20 and WORKPLACES > -20.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility above +2 signals residual stay-at-home behavior that suppresses trips to retail and recreation venues; renewed home-centered activity therefore drives RETAIL_REC lower over the next 7 days.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL weekly mean rises above +2 percent change from baseline.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 7 days is higher than its prior 7-day mean when RESIDENTIAL is above +2.
